  "material_findings": [
    {
      "id": "F1",
      "title": "Deletion/addition asserted from double parentheses without uncertainty",
      "unit_ids": [94, 95],
      "source_quotes": ["(d) ((Not charge tuition or other fees from state-funded eligible students for enrollment in a transition to kindergarten program))Eligible local education agencies are authorized to charge sliding scale fees for enrollment in a transition to kindergarten program, except that no fee may be charged for the following:"],
      "inventory_quotes": ["Deletion shown by double parentheses in proposed WAC 392-425-040(2)(d).", "The proposal deletes WAC 392-425-040's prohibition on charging tuition or other fees to state-funded eligible students for TK enrollment.", "The proposal adds sliding-scale TK enrollment fee authorization to WAC 392-425-040"],
      "severity": "contested",
      "basis": "The plain text contains literal double parentheses and no statement of their meaning; underline markup for new text is absent. The deletion/addition reading follows a WSR convention not evidenced in the supplied text (reference UI-05, UI-06). Both units carry uncertainty 'none'.",
      "practical_implication": "Readers relying on these units take a convention-based interpretation as a source fact. The content of the bracketed text and the authorization sentence are otherwise reported accurately."
    },
    {
      "id": "F2",
      "title": "Truncated or corrupted applicability fields",
      "unit_ids": [88, 95, 96, 98, 99],
      "source_quotes": ["(i) Children who are eligible for but not yet placed in the early childhood education or assistance program or the head start program;", "(e) Tuition and fees collected for students in classrooms receiving state funding for the transition to kindergarten program must be accounted for separately, in accordance with the requirements outlined in the school district accounting manual."],
      "inventory_quotes": ["or head スタ", "or assistance program or head start program, or", "in accordance with the federal individuals with disabilities education ", "school district accounting manual requirem", "this is an age attainment date,"],
      "severity": "known",
      "basis": "Unit 95 applicability ends in two katakana characters not present in the source; units 96, 98, 99 applicability strings end mid-phrase; unit 88 applicability ends with a dangling comma.",
      "practical_implication": "Applicability text for these units is incomplete and in one case contains non-source characters. Assertions themselves are intact. Downstream consumers should not treat these applicability fields as complete condition statements."
    },
    {
      "id": "F3",
      "title": "Eligibility criteria recast as mandatory duties",
      "unit_ids": [86, 87, 85, 88],
      "source_quotes": ["(1) Children meeting the following criteria are eligible to participate in a transition to kindergarten program offered by an eligible local education agency:", "(a) A child who has been determined, by the local education agency, to benefit from additional preparation for kindergarten through a screening process and tool; and", "(b) A child who is at least four years old by August 31st of the school year in which they enroll in a transition to kindergarten program."],
      "inventory_quotes": ["The local education agency must have determined through a screening process and tool that the child benefits from additional preparation for kindergarten.", "A child must be at least four years old by August 31st of the school year of TK enrollment."],
      "severity": "contested",
      "basis": "Source frames (a) and (b) as criteria defining who is eligible; it imposes no 'must' on the LEA to determine or on the child. Units 86 and 87 use 'must' with modality 'mandatory' and uncertainty 'none'. Unit 85 labels eligibility status 'optional'.",
      "practical_implication": "Force labels overstate directive character. Read as conditions of eligibility, the units are accurate; read as duties, they are not evidenced."
    },
    {
      "id": "F4",
      "title": "Declarative-future allocation language labeled mandatory",
      "unit_ids": [102, 103, 104, 110],
      "source_quotes": ["State funding for the transition to kindergarten program will be allocated to eligible local education agencies based on RCW  28A.300.072 and the state omnibus budget requirements. Funding allocations will be prioritized as follows:", "(1) Eligible local education agencies that received state funding allocations for transition to kindergarten in the previous year will have priority for the subsequent year."],
      "inventory_quotes": ["State TK funding will be allocated to eligible local education agencies; the allocating actor is not specified in this provision.", "Prior-year TK funding recipients will have priority for the subsequent year's state funding allocations."],
      "severity": "contested",
      "basis": "Assertion text preserves 'will'; modality field asserts 'mandatory' with uncertainty 'none'. Source uses predictive/declarative 'will be', and the reference recorded it as declarative future with unresolved year frame (UI-10).",
      "practical_implication": "Low. Assertions are faithful; only the modality tag presumes a binding reading."
    },
    {
      "id": "F5",
      "title": "Actor inferred for passive accounting duty",
      "unit_ids": [99],
      "source_quotes": ["(e) Tuition and fees collected for students in classrooms receiving state funding for the transition to kindergarten program must be accounted for separately, in accordance with the requirements outlined in the school district accounting manual.", "(2) In determining student eligibility and admitting students to a transition to kindergarten program, local education agencies must:"],
      "inventory_quotes": ["Local education agencies must account separately for tuition and fees collected for students in state-funded TK classrooms"],
      "severity": "contested",
      "basis": "(e) is passive with no stated actor. The actor is plausibly supplied by the (2) lead-in, but the lead-in's scope is 'determining student eligibility and admitting students', which does not naturally cover accounting. Unit cites only the (e) span.",
      "practical_implication": "Actor assignment is a reasonable inference, not a stated fact. Scope mismatch between lead-in and (e) also bears on UI-07/UI-08."
    },
    {
      "id": "F6",
      "title": "Permissive authorization under a 'must:' lead-in left without uncertainty",
      "unit_ids": [96],
      "source_quotes": ["(2) In determining student eligibility and admitting students to a transition to kindergarten program, local education agencies must:", "Eligible local education agencies are authorized to charge sliding scale fees for enrollment in a transition to kindergarten program, except that no fee may be charged for the following:"],
      "inventory_quotes": ["Eligible local education agencies are authorized to charge sliding scale fees for TK enrollment, subject to the separately stated no-fee exceptions."],
      "severity": "contested",
      "basis": "Modality 'optional' is the most natural reading of 'are authorized', but the sentence is item (d) under a mandatory lead-in and replaces text scoped to 'state-funded eligible students'. Unit records uncertainty 'none'.",
      "practical_implication": "Low to medium. The permissive reading is probably right, but the structural tension and scope shift are unflagged."
    },
    {
      "id": "F7",
      "title": "'or portions of the proposal' omitted from exemption assertions",
      "unit_ids": [71, 72],
      "source_quotes": ["This rule proposal, or portions of the proposal, is exempt from requirements of the Regulatory Fairness Act because the proposal:", "Is fully exempt."],
      "inventory_quotes": ["The proposal is exempt from Regulatory Fairness Act requirements."],
      "severity": "known, low",
      "basis": "Template hedge dropped; unit 76 captures the stated full scope, so net meaning is preserved.",
      "practical_implication": "Negligible."
    },
    {
      "id": "F8",
      "title": "LEA category equated with named school types",
      "unit_ids": [49],
      "source_quotes": ["Local education agencies require timely rules regarding sliding scale fees and state funding allocation criteria in order to conduct enrollment, staffing, budgeting, and program planning activities prior to the start of the school year.", "Timely rule adoption is needed so districts, charter schools, and state-tribal education compact schools can plan for enrollment, staffing, budgeting, and implementation for the 2027-28 school year."],
      "inventory_quotes": ["local education agencies, including districts, charter schools, and state-tribal education compact schools"],
      "severity": "known, low",
      "basis": "Source never states that the three school types are LEAs; the relationship is inferred from parallel sentences.",
      "practical_implication": "Minor inference; likely correct in domain but not in text."
    },
    {
      "id": "F9",
      "title": "Historical filing described as the thing being amended",
      "unit_ids": [81],
      "source_quotes": ["AMENDATORY SECTION(Amending WSR 24-14-074, filed 6/28/24, effective 7/29/24)", "WAC 392-425-040Student eligibility."],
      "inventory_quotes": ["WSR 24-14-074 is identified as the historical filing being amended in the amendatory heading."],
      "severity": "contested, low",
      "basis": "Literal heading reads 'Amending WSR 24-14-074', so the unit is a faithful report of the heading. Semantically the amendment target is WAC 392-425-040 as last set by that filing; unit 84 states the target correctly.",
      "practical_implication": "Readers should pair 81 with 84 to avoid treating the WSR number as the regulated text."
    },
    {
      "id": "F10",
      "title": "Unflagged source ambiguities",
      "unit_ids": [16, 17, 91, 103, 110],
      "source_quotes": ["Participation link available on office of superintendent of public instruction's (OPSI) rules web page at ospi.k12.wa.us/policy-funding/ospi-rulemaking-activity.", "(b) Give priority to children with the lowest family income not otherwise eligible and not enrolled in another local program.", "(d) Data available measuring access to state-funded early learning programs; and"],
      "inventory_quotes": ["The agency rules web page is ospi.k12.wa.us/policy-funding/ospi-rulemaking-activity.", "children not otherwise eligible and not enrolled in another local program.", "permitting individual criteria or combinations without specifying selection or weights"],
      "severity": "known, low",
      "basis": "The 'OPSI' variant, the undefined referent of 'not otherwise eligible', the undefined year frame in 065(1), and the 'one or more' versus list-final 'and' tension are all present in source and absent from inventory uncertainty fields (reference UI-01, UI-09, UI-10).",
      "practical_implication": "Facts are not wrong; uncertainty coverage is thinner than the source warrants."
    }
  ],
  "caveats_and_conclusion": {
    "reference_limitations": [
      "The frozen reference treats the deletion reading of double parentheses as unresolved; a reader applying standard WSR drafting conventions would regard units 94 and 95 as correct. The finding F1 is about evidentiary basis, not likely truth.",
      "The reference's own force labels (declarative future for 065; permissive for 040(2)(d)) are interpretations; F4 and F6 record disagreement in uncertainty handling, not established error.",
      "Reference assigned no unit-level duty to LEAs for (e) because the source is passive; F5 could be resolved either way by a legal reader."
    ],
    "unresolved": [
      "Meaning of double parentheses and status of undecorated text in WAC 392-425-040 (UI-05, UI-06).",
      "Whether 040(2)(d) is permissive, mandatory-framed, or both (UI-07) and its scope relative to 'state-funded eligible students' (UI-08).",
      "Timezone and receipt/postmark basis for all clocks and deadlines (UI-02, UI-03).",
      "Function of the unlabeled 'September 8, 2026' and of 'RDS-7285.3' (UI-04, ID-09)."
    ],
    "overall_conclusion": "Every source function in the frozen reference maps to at least one inventory unit, and the large majority of the 110 assertions are entailed by the quoted source text with appropriate absence statements for timezone, access details, and deadline basis. Material concerns are concentrated in the proposed rule text: deletion/addition asserted from plain-text brackets without uncertainty (94, 95), eligibility criteria and declarative-future language tagged as mandatory duties (86, 87, 102, 103, 104, 110), an inferred actor for the passive accounting duty (99), and five applicability fields that are truncated or contain non-source characters (88, 95, 96, 98, 99). Notice-side units (1 through 84) are substantively sound, with only low-severity glosses and one conflation of historical filing with amendment target (81). This is an advisory assessment; no score is given and completeness of the inventory against the source is not certified."
  }
}

    "reference_limitations": [
      "The frozen reference treats the deletion reading of double parentheses as unresolved; a reader applying standard WSR drafting conventions would regard units 94 and 95 as correct. The finding F1 is about evidentiary basis, not likely truth.",

      "Reference assigned no unit-level duty to LEAs for (e) because the source is passive; F5 could be resolved either way by a legal reader."
    ],
    "unresolved": [
      "Meaning of double parentheses and status of undecorated text in WAC 392-425-040 (UI-05, UI-06).",
      "Whether 040(2)(d) is permissive, mandatory-framed, or both (UI-07) and its scope relative to 'state-funded eligible students' (UI-08).",
      "Timezone and receipt/postmark basis for all clocks and deadlines (UI-02, UI-03).",
      "Function of the unlabeled 'September 8, 2026' and of 'RDS-7285.3' (UI-04, ID-09)."
    ],
    "overall_conclusion": "Every source function in the frozen reference maps to at least one inventory unit, and the large majority of the 110 assertions are entailed by the quoted source text with appropriate absence statements for timezone, access details, and deadline basis. Material concerns are concentrated in the proposed rule text: deletion/addition asserted from plain-text brackets without uncertainty (94, 95), eligibility criteria and declarative-future language tagged as mandatory duties (86, 87, 102, 103, 104, 110), an inferred actor for the passive accounting duty (99), and five applicability fields that are truncated or contain non-source characters (88, 95, 96, 98, 99). Notice-side units (1 through 84) are substantively sound, with only low-severity glosses and one conflation of historical filing with amendment target (81). This is an advisory assessment; no score is given and completeness of the inventory against the source is not certified."
